decisions.evidence: Read every step against Repicky Lemma 2. The row-enlargement of 1.2, the reduction of a counterexample tuple to ground indices via the membership clause, the injectivity and the k-bound of step 2.1, the disjoint transposition automorphism and the compatibility of p with pi r in 3.1, and the closing contradiction in 4.1 were each checked; the sub-box consequence in 5.1 correctly keeps the u-coordinates and discards the rest. No Choice is used beyond finitely many explicit extensions.

Checked the reduction of the finite conjunction to one formula with fixed ordinal and supported parameters, the application of the schema to the concatenated tuple f followed by F, the discarding of the f-clopens, the shrinking inside prescribed neighbourhoods, and the coherence of replacing each t by g o t (injectivity of g from pairwise disjointness). Matches Repicky Corollary 3. The set-difference and complement conventions are declared from their definition suppliers.

Checked the definable well-order of the proper ideals definable from A,f via least definition codes, the unique recursion taking J_xi iff it contains the current ideal, preservation of propriety at successors and limits, and the final maximality argument (I_beta subset I subset J_beta forces I_{beta+1}=J_beta hence J_beta subset I). The statement claims maximality only within the supported definability class, exactly as the source gap noted at Step 3b requires; no Zorn or choice is used.

Read against the recovered source arXiv:2511.21684 (HTML). The statement is the filter-extension property of Ransom Def 3.8/Thm 4.1 with K=fix(E); step 1.3 is Ransom Lemma 4.5, the Todorcevic-Farah compatible-type lemma derived in Appendix C by flattening a fixed type into C_theta; 1.4 is Lemma 4.3 from Erdos-Rado; 1.5 is the Sigma/Gamma spreading and gathering of Section 5.1; 2.1-4.1 are the Harrington-style search-and-shift with the D=empty case handled separately; 5.1 restores the countable index set by Theorems 5.23/5.27 and Corollary 5.28 over Coll(omega,Theta); 6.1 iterates the extension along the ground well-order of the HS names for subsets of X. Verified the support-restriction lemma, the distinguishing strengthening, the constant-color thinning, the compatibility chain, and the orbit subfamily argument. Ground AC is confined to the metatheoretic steps declared in A1.

Composition item checked: F1/F2 supply the same finite-support symmetric presentation for which the filter-extension property is proved, so the BPI clause follows, and the failure-of-choice clause cites a published item about the same orbit set A (well-order would enumerate least unused members, contradicting Dedekind-finiteness). The ground-model AC is explicitly metatheoretic and not ascribed to N; no use is made of the unsupported parameter-definable maximal-ideal shortcut.

Checked the finite-refutation reduction: one target refutation uses finitely many ZF schema instances plus BPI and not-AC; the fragment lemma supplies a set model of those instances; the search-and-shift item is one fixed finite ZFC proof; relativizing the refutation and appending the finite satisfaction induction yields a finite ZFC contradiction, which the published transfer theorem converts from Con(ZF) to Con(ZFC+GCH). No PA-uniform selector, completeness theorem, or countable transitive model is assumed.

Checked the finite expansion induction (empty case e_empty=1; successor case using distributivity of join over meet), the resulting identity 1 = join of the truth-assignment atoms, and the two-case reduction of the clopen-pattern hypotheses to atoms lying below an ideal member. The example correctly states that it does not assert the unresolved A-page primality lemma constructed such a pattern.

Checked both halves: AC implies BPI is a published ZF theorem, and strictness is claimed only conditionally on Con(ZF) through the consistency of ZF+BPI+not-AC proved on this page. The model alternative (Dedekind-finite coordinate set) is cited from the accepted model theorem, and the consistency antecedent is part of the displayed claim.

Definition checked against Jech Theorem 10.6: finite partial functions on omega times omega with p(n,i)<aleph_n, restriction to initial layers, the layer-preserving permutation group acting on the i-coordinates, the normal subgroups H_m fixing layers below m and their upward closure as a normal filter. The ground AC/GCH use is declared and confined to the ground cardinal calculations, and no Choice is ascribed to the resulting symmetric model.

Checked that hereditary symmetry gives some H_m inside the stabilizer, that the Boolean nice name with coefficients ||k in x|| has the same value, and that H_m fixes k-check names and x-dot hence each coefficient; the resulting name is hereditarily symmetric with bounded layer support. The single H_m is chosen for one fixed name, not simultaneously for a family.

Checked the proof of Jech Lemma 10.7: for p at or below u with p restricted below m not below u, density gives q below the restriction and below not-u; a finite coordinate move in each upper layer makes p and pi q compatible; H_m-fixedness transports q not below not-u to pi q, and the common extension contradicts Boolean incompatibility. The join identity and the identification of B_m with the complete subalgebra generated by initial-layer conditions follow, including m=0.

Definition checked: S_m is the ground set of Boolean names for subsets of omega with coefficients in B_m, R_m its interpretation, H_m fixes each such name so every member is hereditarily symmetric, and normality of H_m in the layer-preserving group makes the S_m and the sequence of layers canonical symmetric names. No choice principle is used.

Checked the cardinal estimates: |P_<m| <= aleph_m, so |B_m| <= 2^{aleph_m} = aleph_{m+1} under GCH, and |S_m| <= (2^{aleph_m})^{aleph_0} = aleph_{m+1}; a single ground surjection e_m is interpreted by an H_m-fixed canonical name whose interpretation is a surjection from the ground ordinal aleph_{m+1}^V onto R_m in N. The use of ground AC/GCH is declared and covers m=0.

Checked that the generic union of layer n is a total surjection omega onto aleph_n^V (functionality from compatibility, totality and surjectivity from dense sets), that its canonical name is fixed by H_{n+1} and hence in N, and that a surjection onto a nonempty set yields an injection by least preimages inside N. The construction is for one fixed n and does not claim the sequence of maps is in N.

Checked the composition g_m = e_m o f_{m+1} of the two supplied N-maps, the least-preimage argument giving an injection from R_m into omega in N, and the explicit refusal to choose enumerations for the whole family. Boundary case m=0 uses f_1 and the coarse bound of the preceding lemma.

Checked both inclusions: every real has a bounded-layer Boolean name so lies in some R_m, and every R_m consists of reals of N; the sequence of layers itself is a set of N, so Union in N forms the countable union, and each layer is countable there. The theorem deliberately avoids selecting simultaneous enumerations.

Checked the internal application of the ZF uncountability of R (nested-interval construction, no Choice) inside N, combined with the countable-union identity. The contrast is stated without inferring that the union is countable.

Checked the two directions: every ordinal below aleph_omega^V is below some aleph_n^V hence countable in N (finite ordinals by hand, the rest by restricting the layer surjection); and a supposed N-surjection omega onto kappa=aleph_omega^V would, using an H_m-fixed name, put the H_m-fixed Boolean values in B_m, so each A_k = set of alpha with a lower-layer witness is bounded by aleph_m^V while the surjectivity makes kappa the union of the A_k - a contradiction. The leastness argument then gives omega_1^N = kappa. Ground AC is used only for the cardinal count of P_<m.

Checked the explicit ground cofinal sequence n -> aleph_n^V (a set of V hence of N) and the ZF facts that the cofinality of an infinite limit cardinal is an infinite cardinal bounded by any exhibited cofinal subset, giving cf(omega_1)=omega in N.

Checked the three conclusions: the layer decomposition refutes the countable-union assertion; cf(omega_1)=omega makes omega_1 singular; and the published ZF fact that AC_omega implies cf(omega_1)=omega_1 gives the failure of countable choice. No choice principle is used to derive its own failure, and the definitions are cited.

Checked the finite-proof-tracing claim: a fixed finite target fragment expands to finitely many source instances, the transfer lemma supplies a countable transitive reflected source and generic, and the retained HS verification gives a set interpretation satisfying the fragment plus the three displayed sentences. The quantification over fragments is metatheoretic, no uniform truth predicate is claimed, and ambient AC enters only through the reflected source.

Checked the finite-refutation argument from the finite formalization lemma and the published Con(ZF) -> Con(ZFC+GCH) transfer; no set model of full ZF, completeness theorem, or transitive-model hypothesis is used, and the conclusion is the stated conditional consistency.

Checked the definition: bit-flip action by arbitrary elements of 2^{omega times omega}, the normal subgroups H_m fixing the first m layers, the ranked classes M_m of sets hereditarily definable from ordinals and the predicates S_0..S_{m-1}, and the union M*. Verified that the identification M* = HS^G_F is correct: an H_m-fixed Boolean value projects to a join of conditions restricted to layers below m (the orbit join of a condition equals its initial-layer restriction), so values of H_m-fixed names lie in the submodel generated by the first m predicates and, conversely, finite-predicate definitions have H_m-fixed canonical names. The non-membership of the full predicate sequence is argued correctly by the tail flip of S_m.

Checked the transfer through the identification of the definition item and the published HS-model theorem, including the concrete schema explanation (finitely many parameters fit in one stage; the hereditary recursion keeps members in the union) and the declared Choice boundary (ground V=L only).

Checked the construction: D = the finite set of second coordinates used at layer n+1 in the condition Q, k_0 = 1+max D, the flip a on the tail of coordinate n+1 induces an order automorphism, it fixes Q and every parameter of a definition using only S_0..S_n and ordinals, and it sends S_{n+1} to its complement modulo exactly the finite initial segment k_0. The finite/infinite distinction in 3.1 is correct.

Checked the proof of Feferman Theorem 4.12: a nonprincipal prime ideal contains every finite set; for the fresh predicate A = S_{n+1} primality selects a side C, a condition Q forces C in I and the definition of I; the tail flip fixes Q, the parameters of the definition, and I, so Q also forces pi(C) in I; pi(C) differs finitely from the complement of C, the finite difference lies in I, and downward closure puts the complement in I, forcing omega into I. Both choices of C and the finite-modification steps were checked.

Checked the duality between ultrafilters and prime ideals: maximality decides every subset, the complement set is a proper prime ideal, and principalness of that ideal makes U the principal ultrafilter at k. The argument covers the empty and whole-set cases through the ideal conventions.

Checked the cofinite filter (proper, upward closed, closed under finite intersections), the extension given by the internal UFL/BPI equivalence, and the contradiction with the no-free-ultrafilter theorem since an extension of the cofinite filter is free. The equivalence supplier is a ZF theorem, so both BPI and UFL fail in the model.

Checked the finite-proof-tracing argument for Feferman's model: finitely many source instances, the reflected source and generic from the transfer lemma, the retained tail-complement and cofinite-filter instances, and the resulting set model of the fragment plus the two extra sentences. Ambient AC is used only for the reflected source, and no uniform truth predicate is claimed.

Checked the finite-refutation reduction using the finite formalizability lemma and the published consistency transfer; the conclusion is the stated conditional consistency of ZF with all-ultrafilters-on-omega-principal and not-BPI.

Checked the syntactic argument from the consistent countertheory T = ZF + every ultrafilter on omega is principal + not-BPI and the published ZF equivalence of BPI with the set ultrafilter lemma; both nonprovability conclusions are conditional on Con(ZF) and use no completeness theorem.

Checked against Tachtsis pp.5-7: the Cohen forcing Fn(omega times omega,2), the generic reals a_n, the finite-modification classes delta(x), f(n) = {delta(a_n), delta(omega minus a_n)}, S = union of the classes together with f, and the parameter-HOD class N of sets hereditarily definable from f, finitely many members of S minus f and ordinals. Since S is definable from f and each member of S minus f is a real, the proof language of 'finitely many reals s_i' is faithful to the source; the model is not identified with Feferman's, and the relativized HOD check is flagged as required.

Checked the Tachtsis Theorem 4 argument: independence gives infinite symmetric differences so the classes are distinct and the pairs disjoint; a supposed choice function c on an infinite subfamily would be definable from f, ordinals and finitely many reals s_i in S minus f, each a finite modification of some a_{m_i}; choosing the least k outside the finite set of indices, the tail flip of coordinate k fixes p, every s_i, ordinals and f (it swaps the two members of the pair f(k)) while interchanging delta(a_k) and delta(omega minus a_k); applying the symmetry lemma forces both values of c at f(k), contradicting functionality. Finite choices are not excluded, and no ultrafilter claim is used.

Read all steps of this rendering of the no-new-measurables half of the Levy-Solovay/gap-forcing theorem with the local definition of measurability (nonprincipal, closed under intersections of length below kappa): uniformity, regularity and strong-limit of a measure; the ultrapower, normality, seed and kappa-closure facts of 1.2; the delta-gap set-up; the fresh-sequence obstruction 4.1; the alternating cover argument 4.2 and the common delta-sequences claim 5.1; the two inductions 6.1 and 7.1; the amenability argument 7.2; and the ground measure U_0 of 8.1, which is nonprincipal and kappa-complete by elementarity and uniformity. Choice is used in the ground and in the ultrapower, never inside a target inner model. The statement is the classical theorem, and the rendering follows the cited gap-forcing structure.

Checked every numbered step. Step 1.1's ZF verification for the parameter-HOD class follows the standard HOD checks relativized to f and a finite parameter reservoir. Steps 2.1-3.1 exclude free ultrafilters on omega by the fresh-coordinate tail flip (it fixes p, every s_i, all ordinals and the pair-valued f, and maps a member of U to a finite modification of its complement). Steps 4.1-5.1 are N-internal: minimality of kappa, uniformity and kappa-completeness via the least-partition argument. In 6.1-8.1 the intermediate model V_0 = L[a_k : k in K] is contained in N because every element of L[c] is hereditarily definable from the finitely many reals c and ordinals and each a_k lies in S; the residual quotient is weakly homogeneous by finite flips fixing the parameters, so U restricted to P(kappa)^{V_0} is a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter in V_0 = M[G restricted to K], a countable forcing extension of L, contradicting V=L through the small-forcing theorem and Scott's argument. The W-hierarchy in 9.1-13.1, closure facts 10.1-11.1 and the two inductions 12.1/13.1 were checked. Only a technical reading is needed at 6.1: 'decided by the top condition' is to be read as 'decided by a condition of the generic that forces uniqueness of the defining formula', which is the standard reduction.

Checked the finite-proof tracing: the target fragment plus the all-ultrafilters sentence has a finite source expansion; the constructible-interpretation translator supplies the finite ZF fragment; the reflected countable transitive source with its generic yields a set-sized parameter-HOD structure satisfying the selected formulas, including the all-ultrafilters sentence. No uniform truth predicate or set model of full ZF is claimed, and ambient AC is confined to the reflected source and the stated source-side cardinal arguments.

Checked the finite-refutation argument from the preceding formalization lemma and the published transfer of Con(ZF) to Con(ZFC+GCH); the conclusion is conditional syntactic consistency with no completeness or transitive-model step.

Checked the explicit first layers (H_0 = the whole group, so R_0 uses no collapse layer, R_1 layer 0, R_2 layers 0 and 1), the three specified maps g_m = e_m o f_{m+1}, and the contradiction from a hypothetical simultaneous enumeration of all layers (Cantor pairing would make R countable). The example exhibits the exact role of simultaneous countable choice.

Checked the refutation inside the consistent Feferman-Levy theory: the layer sequence is pointwise countable with union the whole real line, while ZF proves the line uncountable, so the false statement cannot be a ZF theorem. The boundary note excludes the empty/one-set degenerate readings and no enumeration is selected from the family.

Checked the refutation from the consistent theory with cf(omega_1)=omega, the ZF inequality omega not equal omega_1, and the definition of regularity; the degenerate equality is excluded inside ZF and the conclusion is conditional on Con(ZF).

Checked the coordinate calculation: the flipped set is disjoint from the domain of the condition, so the condition is fixed; below k_0 membership is preserved and above it reversed, so the symmetric difference with the complement is exactly the finite initial segment k_0. The k_0=0 and k_0=1 cases are covered.

Checked the invariance calculation: a free ultrafilter contains no finite set (else a singleton would be principal), so every cofinite set is in U, and membership is invariant under finite symmetric difference via the cofinite agreement set. The example correctly contrasts this with the infinite tail flip and covers X=empty, X=omega and X=Y.

Checked the fresh-coordinate tail flip: it fixes the condition, ordinals and the parameter reals, swaps the two members of f(k) while fixing the unordered pair and every other value, so a supposed choice function would take two distinct values at f(k). The example correctly restricts the obstruction to infinite subfamilies and makes no ultrafilter claim.

Definition checked: finitistic tree with finite levels and no terminal nodes (so every node has extensions at all greater finite heights by finite recursion), height as the cardinality of the finite strict predecessor set, the (h,k)-density notion with the stated k=0 and empty-set boundary cases, and the distinction between the full product, the level product and matrices, which need not lie in the level product. The two cone-restriction consequences are correct, including the common-maximum-height step for finitely many roots; d=0 is excluded.

Definition checked: the language L_d of length-2d words with exactly one legal ordered pair per coordinate, the three one-step rule classes (elementary commutation, matched-pair replacement, adjacent finite block permutation) with their side conditions, and the reflexive-transitive closure. The definition is purely syntactic and asserts no semantics, as required before the soundness lemma.

Verified the induction: the bridge derivation of 1.1 uses only Rule 3, Rule 1 and Rule 2 steps (checked the instance for the displayed words), 1.2's lifting of a (d-1)-derivation through either outside matched pair is a finite induction on derivation length after the Rule 3 rearrangement, and 1.3 is the Rule 2 base. Every displayed intermediate word keeps one legal ordered pair per coordinate, and 2.1 assembles the induction with two lifting applications.

Checked the semantic scheme and all three rules: Rule 1 pointwise; Rule 2 by collecting finitely many cone witnesses and conversely by taking a dense set's member in each cone (finite, no choice); Rule 3 by the finite back-and-forth over the m = product of level sizes, with the increasing least-witness recursion p_j = G(m-j) and monotonicity preserving earlier tuples, and with n_i-density recovered from p_m-density. The derivation-length induction in 6.1 is finite.

Checked the case split on the quantified endpoint scheme: when it holds, the derived word supplies k-dense coordinate sets whose product lies in Q; when it fails, some level vector and p = h+k yield cone roots whose products avoid Q, and extending the finitely many roots to the common height h gives (h,k)-dense sets in the complement. Both alternatives and the k=0 case were checked; only finitely many cone roots are extended, so the proof stays in ZF.

Checked the induction on the number of colours, the bad-colouring tree with finite levels and nodes at every level, the appeal to Konig's lemma under the declared AC, and both dichotomy cases: the last colour's (h,1)-matrix thins into a truncation, contrarily to badness; a k-matrix inside the union of the first q colours pulls back along finite dominating maps and the induction hypothesis produces a monochromatic (h,1)-matrix inside the same truncation. The terminal common-level form uses the same pullback along extension maps.

Definition checked: a finite partial prime-ideal diagram is a Boolean homomorphism on a finite subalgebra, its zero fibre is a proper prime ideal, and requiring the domain to be the generated finite subalgebra (cells as atoms, zero cells discarded) records every Boolean consequence among the listed elements. The empty list and repetitions are handled explicitly.

Checked the finite atom argument: the unique A-atom with value 1, a nonzero C-atom below it, the homomorphism e'(x)=1 iff c<=x, preservation of the Boolean operations, and the agreement with e on A. The extension to any prescribed finite subset follows by taking the generated finite subalgebra. All selections are from single finite nonempty sets.

Checked the tree of homomorphisms on the finite generated subalgebras of an enumerated Boolean algebra: finite levels, a node at every level by the finite extension lemma, and the ZF definable good-successor recursion (a good node has a good immediate successor because finitely many successors with finite bounds would bound the parent), which avoids both choice and Konig's lemma. The union homomorphism is well defined modulo repetitions, and the equivalence with enumerated finite satisfiability was checked in both directions, including properness of the generated ideal.

Checked both implications. BPI implies UFL via the complement ideal I_F, the quotient algebra, a prime ideal P, and the prime ideal J of P(S) above I_F, whose complement filter is maximal; UFL implies BPI via the set X of finite partial homomorphisms, the finite intersection property of the deciding sets D_b, the extension to an ultrafilter V, and the homomorphism h read off from the chosen cells, with finite Boolean equations decided by a set in V. Boundary cases: the empty S (no proper filter) and the trivial algebra are excluded as in the definition.

Composition item checked: the ZF dichotomy clause is stated with no construction hypothesis, and the model clause cites the accepted basic Cohen theorem in the same hereditarily symmetric presentation; the two axiom bases are kept separate as declared.

Checked the conservative-extension argument: a hypothetical refutation of the target uses finitely many HL instances which are replaced by their fixed ZF derivations, yielding a refutation of ZF+BPI+not-AC, contradicting the accepted consistency corollary. The conclusion is the stated conditional Con implication.

Checked both directions: the consistent BPI+not-AC extension comes from the finite-refutation reduction; the Feferman model with all ultrafilters on omega principal refutes BPI through the cofinite filter, since BPI would extend it to a free ultrafilter. Both claims carry the Con(ZF) antecedent and the empty/whole-set cases are handled by the finite-intersection property definitions.

Checked the explicit level-2 product, the (1,2)-dense sets A_1, A_2 with their frontier domination, and the two structural separations: (0,101) is in the full product but not the level product, and A_1 x A_2 is a matrix not contained in the level product.

Checked the repair: roots of heights 1 and 3 are extended to the common height 3, the dense frontiers above the extended roots are (3,k)-dense, and the k=2 and k=0 instances are computed explicitly. The final general remark correctly derives the density from any (3+k)-dense set.

Replayed all ten displayed rule applications and verified that each intermediate word lies in L_2 and that each step is an instance of Rule 1, Rule 2 (in either direction) or Rule 3 with the stated r and permutation.

Checked the enumeration of the finite-cofinite algebra, the generated subalgebras at the first levels, the branch selecting the cofinite remainder, and the resulting homomorphism h(A)=0 iff A finite, whose zero fibre Fin is a proper prime ideal.

Checked the unconditional model argument (a well-order of the infinite Dedekind-finite set A would either stop, making A finite, or inject omega into A) and the conditional syntactic reading through the consistency of ZF+BPI+not-AC. The consistency antecedent is stated.

Definition checked: the constructible ground L^U is ZFC+V=L with the same ordinals and keeps kappa inaccessible (downward absoluteness of regularity, cardinals below kappa computed in the inner model, GCH giving the strong limit); P = Lv(kappa) is the finite-condition collapse with p(alpha,n) < alpha; the initial restrictions are complete projections with quotient factorizations; and the text asserts no model or generic existence and keeps Choice on the ground/ambient side.

Checked the three clauses: kappa = omega_1 in V[G] (every smaller ordinal is collapsed, kappa survives the kappa-cc); each name for an omega-sequence of ordinals is decided by countably many maximal antichains of size below kappa whose finite supports are bounded by regularity, so the sequence already lies in some V[G_xi]; and the tail collapse makes the ground-small set of nice P_xi-names for reals countable in V[G], giving the required surjection. Ambient AC selects the antichains only.

Checked the three assertions: the small-collapse factorization to V[F] with a generic collapsing map, the real t coding the preorder reconstructing lambda and F so that V[F]=V[t] and f is definable from (t,beta) via the constructible ground's canonical well-order; the absorption recursion of the initial forcing and the tail into a fresh Lv(kappa) over V[f]; and weak homogeneity of the collapse (moving the finitely many coordinates of one condition off the other), which fixes every parameter in V[f] so H-free sentences get Boolean value 0 or 1. The random/Cohen variant inserts the small factor first.

Definition checked: S is the class of countable ordinal sequences, OD(S) uses one member of S plus finitely many ordinals and a rank-bounded unique definition, and M = HOD(S) is hereditary in that predicate. The coding remark (countable tuples of S-members interleave into one member, reals are members of S after coding) is correct, and no equality with L(R) or HOD(R) is asserted.

Definition checked: the L(R) hierarchy with the ambient reals as parameters, limit unions, the identification as the least transitive inner model containing all ordinals and reals, and the induction showing L(R) is contained in HOD(S) because each real parameter is a member of S. The reverse inclusion and the identifications with HOD(R) are explicitly not asserted.

Checked the ZF verification for M=HOD(S) (transitivity, ordinals and reals; Separation by conjoining hereditary definitions; Replacement via ambient images being hereditarily OD(S); Power Set by the uniform predicate on ambient subsets) and the real-parameter reduction: substituting the real-capture definition of the unique S-parameter into the definition of A gives definability from one real and finitely many ordinals, with no claim that M equals L(R) or HOD(R).

Checked the coding argument: a definable surjection F from Ord times S onto M, ambient choice of codes for each f(n), interleaving the countably many S-parameters and ordinals into one member of S, and definability of the graph from that single parameter; the empty and constant cases need no selection.

Checked the DC transfer: an ambient recursive chain built with one choice function on the reals of the model lies in M by the omega-sequence closure lemma, and transitivity makes M compute the relation correctly. The singleton and nonempty cases are covered.

Checked the four assertions: shared well-founded Borel codes evaluate identically on shared reals; coded nullness and meagreness have absolute real/ordinal witnesses; the induction producing a coded open-mod-meagre representative handles complements and countable unions; and coded nonemptiness and perfectness transfer only under shared reals or an explicit pruned splitting-tree certificate, with the new-branch caveat stated. Internal DC is used only for countable closures.

Checked the enumeration of the countably many coded null sets and closed nowhere-dense sets of an intermediate model N, and the identification of the nonrandom and non-generic reals with the union of those sets; absoluteness of the codes makes the union null or meagre. Repeated enumeration covers finite models of codes and empty exceptions.

Checked both cases: the random-algebra Boolean value has an N-coded Borel representative and the truth lemma plus tail homogeneity (no occurrence of H) extends the equivalence with membership to V[G] for every N-random real; the Cohen case gives a regular-open representative with nowhere-dense boundary. The nontrivial partial-coverage caveat for nongenerics is explicit and handled later by coded null/meagre exceptions.

Checked the chain: A in M has a real-plus-ordinals definition, the real localizes to a bounded N, nonrandom reals lie in an N-coded null set, and the random ones satisfy A iff they lie in an N-coded Borel set, so A differs from a Borel set by a null set; absoluteness and internal completeness of the null ideal give measurability. Empty, whole-line and zero-exception cases are covered.

Checked the parallel chain with a coded meagre exception and the open-mod-meagre representative of a Borel set; all codes are reals of M and internal DC closes the meagre ideal under the displayed union, giving BP. U empty and U=R cover the boundary cases.

Checked the simultaneous fusion: enumerations of dense sets of Q and of Q^2 with downward closure, the finite requirement processing with a definable preference-free descent, the splitting lemma (otherwise the name would be forced into N via the definable sequence of decided strings), the branch genericity, pairwise mutual genericity, distinctness of interpretations and continuity of the map; compactness gives a perfect image.

Checked the localization dichotomy: if A were contained in a bounded stage N, an ambient enumeration of the countably many reals of N would give an M-enumeration of A, contradicting internal uncountability, so some x in A minus N exists; a localized name forced new and in A below a condition plus the perfect-tree lemma gives a real-coded compact injective image inside A, which transfers to M by code absoluteness. The countable alternative in the contrapositive uses the same enumeration.

Checked the digit-interleaving transfer: the ambiguity set is a finite union of Borel null sets, the interleaving map is a measure-preserving Borel bijection taking nk-cylinders to products of dyadic intervals, the pullback of an arbitrary set is measurable by the one-dimensional theorem, and completion transfers a Borel-mod-null pair back. Integer cubes cover R^n disjointly and internal DC supplies exactly the countable choice needed by the product-measure interface; the n=1 and n=0 cases are separated.

Checked both contradictions: a measurable Vitali selector is null (rational translate cover makes [0,1] null) or of positive measure (finitely many disjoint translates exceed a containing interval); a Bernstein set and its complement contain no perfect set, and at least one is uncountable because the two-term union of countable sets would otherwise be countable, contradicting PSP. The unsupported 'definition alone makes B uncountable' reading is explicitly replaced.

Checked both reductions: a Hamel basis gives a coefficient homomorphism whose measurable kernel is a proper subgroup, either all of R by positive-measure rigidity or null, when the rational coset cover is null and contradicts lambda([0,1])=1; for additive f the measurable bounded-level sets cover [-1,1], one has positive measure, Steinhaus bounds f near zero and regularity gives f(x)=xf(1). Zero-map and n=0 cases are covered.

Checked the volume calculation: every piece is measurable, a positive-radius ball has 0<V<infinity from inner and outer cubes, finite additivity gives V as the sum of the piece measures, rigid invariance gives the same sum for the reassembly, and two disjoint congruent copies have measure 2V, so V=2V. The radius-zero case is excluded separately.

Checked the reductio: AC in M would relativize the published Bernstein-set construction to M, contradicting the accepted no-Bernstein theorem; the model's DC is compatible with the failure of full AC.

Checked the L(R) verification: transitivity and continuity of the hierarchy, the standard reflection arguments for Separation, Replacement and Power Set, the finite unfolding code giving a definable surjection from Ord times R onto L(R), and the DC construction by ordinal minimization plus one ambient choice function on the model's reals, with the chain recovered from one interleaved real. No well-order of the reals or internal AC is assumed.
